//: forceExit is retained deliberately and is NOT masking an app leak. --detectOpenHandles across a diverse spec sample (mcp-health, scoped-pool, staleness-event, communities, fact-usage, concurrent-single-active) reports ZERO open handles: app.close() + the OnModuleDestroy hooks (SurrealService et al.) release every resource, so the suite exits cleanly on its own. forceExit stays as the CI-termination backstop that pairs with workerIdleMemoryLimit below: an over-budget worker can be hard-killed (the #78 SIGABRT root cause), and forceExit guarantees the jest parent still terminates instead of hanging the runner. Drop it only after a FULL-suite run without it confirms every spec exits cleanly.
//ci: Serial (maxWorkers 1) on purpose. The in-process e2e loads native modules (bge-m3 ONNX ~340MB + cross-encoder) per worker; at 50% (=2 on the 4CPU/16GB CI runner) two heavy full-stack suites (memory-injection-redteam / fovea-cascade / memtrap) coexist and exhaust RAM, so the OS SIGABRT-kills a worker (Napi::Error, 'suite failed to run' while every test that ran passed). Recurred after the #344 maxWorkers:50% attempt on memory-injection-redteam specifically. Serial gives each suite the full runner memory; workerIdleMemoryLimit still restarts the worker between files to free native allocations. Locally (more RAM) the full e2e is green at any worker count; this is a CI-memory constraint, not a test bug.
